key_insight: Evolution Strategy can directly learn a recurrent wall controller on a large turbulent channel and achieve stronger drag reduction than prior learned control, avoiding the small-box degeneracies seen in gradient-based policies.
engineering_relevance: This suggests that gradient-free, episode-level optimization can produce more robust closed-loop wall actuation strategies for practical turbulent drag-reduction systems.
method: Optimize a recurrent closed-loop controller with Evolution Strategy on a full-size turbulent channel at Re_τ≈180.
Evaluate each candidate policy over complete flow episodes using an energy-aware reward.
Analyze friction, Reynolds stresses, and anisotropy to compare how the controller reshapes near-wall turbulence.
evidence_signal: On the large-domain test, the ES controller reduced skin-friction drag by about 26%, outperforming GRU-MARL trained on a minimal box (17%) and slightly exceeding opposition control (22%).
watch_item: The result is demonstrated at Re_τ≈180 in simulation, so transfer to higher Reynolds numbers, different geometries, and real hardware still needs validation.
paper_title: Gradient-free learning of a closed-loop wall controller for turbulent drag reduction
